title: Becoming swing-conscious and imitating society bands like the Castle Lomas
summary: Between 1937 and the early forties hillbilly bands moved to more elaborate voicing. Parker names Abe Lyman, Casa Loma and Callaway as the models, since they made near-jazz records.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: I'm here. Did you ever hear the name Cliff Gross, the hillbilly violinist Cliff Gross, who came from Kentucky, who had been with us earlier. But even while I was with the Dubois, in the 1937 to 40, I kept hanging around there, you got to stretch that 40 to around 42, because I would still play radio programs in the afternoon and side dates with members of the band, and records with Boyd. But during that period of time, the format changed a great deal as the hillbilly musicians became swing conscious, and as that status symbol forced us into more elaborate voicing and orchestration. It started out though just as plain simple voicing of two violins, even in those days in the guitar before. And then gradually we found our place subservient to those two.
You were trying for more elaborate arrangements. And then we found out who were you imitating or trying to come up to.

Well, even I remember something, was it a long time ago with Blackish Simmons, as early as Abe Lyman, Weary Weasel. Do you remember that? And that sort of thing. And the old Castle Lomas used to have kind of swing records for Brunswick a long time ago. And we liked them. This was society bands. Well I know, but they had all kinds of sometimes swing records that came out. Yes. Before this. This is before the word swing now.
Yes, but even in the early, very early Castle Lomas, some of their records were very close to jazz. Do you have any of those here? You know anything about those, Paul?
I don't know that I've heard.
Put on your old great body and the Alexander's Ragtime Band, I remember especially, by Castle Lomas.
I don't know. But there were some guys.
There were some, there were guys around that were playing, I mean, 33, 31, 32, 33.
These were the kind of bands that you in a sense were trying to come up to.
